hardware: linux x64; AMD Ryzen 7 7435HS; 24.9 GB RAM; GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU (6GB VRAM)
methodology: Backend: Ollama local inference. Order: deterministic prompt-file order; A = forced heavy/no-cache, B = auto/no-cache, C = auto/cache-on over two full passes. Warm-up: before each run, one unmeasured forced-heavy request is completed; identical prompt and sampling settings are used. Cache is flushed before each run; for C it remains enabled for both passes. Cache results include labeled duplicate prompts. Latency is measured at the gateway from the successful request attempt through terminal SSE event; rate-limit backoff is excluded from per-request latency but included in total wall time. Router TTFT/tokens-per-second are reported from final usage metadata. Swap count is a proxy for non-cache-hit inference requests with positive final-chunk load_ms; it is not an independent hardware swap counter. Routing accuracy and confusion matrix use the dry-run preview endpoint and expected tiers in prompts.json; this is not answer-quality evaluation. GPU/VRAM values are omitted when the stats contract reports them as unavailable. Mock-backend measurements are for smoke testing only and are not hardware performance claims.
verdict: Router reduced mean latency by 24.3% vs heavy-only (KPI-2 target of 30% lower not met).

kpis.note: Only KPI-1 and the A/B latency comparison are measured by this harness; other KPIs require their dedicated instrumentation and comparison run.
